channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Why are Europe’s cancer organisations targeting nicotine?
item.description: Cancer prevention depends on identifying the exposures that drive disease burden. In tobacco use, the principal risk arises from combustion and the resulting toxicants, rather than nicotine itself. Conflating nicotine with smoking can weaken public understanding of relative risk and obscure the potential role of smoke-free alternatives for adults who continue to smoke. Public health communication should distinguish clearly between dependence, exposure and disease causation. (Published on September 30, 2026bysnusforumet.se)

item.title: Growing evidence supports nicotine pouches as an alternative to smoking
item.description: The evidence base for nicotine pouches is becoming harder to dismiss as a niche issue. As smoke-free, non-combustible products, pouches may offer adult smokers another route away from cigarettes, particularly where acceptability and everyday use matter. Their role should be assessed through toxicology, switching behaviour and population-level impact rather than moral discomfort with nicotine. A credible tobacco policy should ask whether these products reduce exposure to the harms of smoking — and regulate them accordingly. (Published on September 30, 2026byquitlikesweden.org)

item.title: Good news: The proportion of young smokers is declining in Switzerland
item.description: A decline in young people smoking should be treated as good news — and as a reason to look carefully at what is changing. Falling smoking rates suggest that newer nicotine patterns do not automatically translate into more cigarette use, which challenges one of the strongest arguments against harm reduction. The priority now should be keeping youth smoking low while ensuring adult smokers are not denied lower-risk routes away from combustion. Policy should follow the trend, not the fear that the trend contradicts. (Published on September 30, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: The mendacity of ASH
item.description: Trust is fragile when public health organisations appear to bend evidence around a preferred message. In tobacco policy, that matters because smokers rely on official voices to understand the difference between cigarettes, vaping, pouches and other lower-risk products. Selective claims may win a debate in the short term, but they can weaken confidence in the institutions meant to guide people away from harm. Honest communication should be able to defend tobacco control without distorting harm reduction. (Published on October 01, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: The FDA Promises To Streamline the Dauntingly Complex Rules for Approving Nicotine Products
item.description: Regulatory complexity has become part of the nicotine problem. A system too slow or difficult to navigate can leave legal smoke-free products waiting while cigarettes remain on shelves and unapproved alternatives fill the gaps. Streamlining FDA approvals would not mean lowering the evidentiary bar; it would mean making science-based decisions in time to matter. Harm reduction needs a pathway that is rigorous, workable and capable of bringing responsible products into the legal market. (Published on October 01, 2026byreason.com)
